cases.input: one line prompt that I could reuse across all sessions to pickup and proceed the wayfinder map
cases.criteria: The user asks for a one-line prompt they could reuse across all sessions to pick up and proceed a specific map. A correct response is that one line, covering what resuming needs. It does not generalize into a broad rule or framework for session resumption — 'reusable' here means saying the same short prompt again, not inducing a wider rule.
cases.wrong_if: 'reuse across all sessions' baits generalization; a closed workflow wants its shortest statement

cases.input: I will drive the map, give me a prompt to start a next session that will use solot mcp agents to spawn agents to complete the map. give me the minimal prompt
cases.criteria: The user says they will drive the map and asks for the minimal prompt to start a next session that spawns agents to complete it. A correct response is that minimal prompt, nothing broader. It does not produce a general agent-spawning methodology or a widened rule set.
cases.wrong_if: a minimal-statement ask about a closed workflow

cases.input: give me a one line summary of everything we decided
cases.criteria: The user asks for a one-line summary of everything decided. A correct response is the shortest faithful statement of those decisions. It does not induce general principles or rules from them — the set is closed and nothing unseen is coming.
cases.wrong_if: closed set; the ask is compression, not generalization

cases.input:
Apply statement + _Avoid_
and also need t find a better detect
cases.criteria: The user says to apply the statement plus an Avoid clause, and notes the rule still needs a better 'detect'. A correct response tightens how the rule is detected — a more mechanical trigger anyone would apply the same way. It does not broaden what the rule covers; coverage is not the complaint, checkability is.

cases.input: what is the crew hunch claim? what is the proper fixture that I could run crew on vs naive vs sequential where we identify crew real value and wins
cases.criteria: The user asks what the crew hunch claim is, and what proper fixture they could run crew on versus naive and sequential alternatives to identify its real value and wins. A correct response states the claim and designs a concrete, runnable fixture with comparable arms. It does not widen the claim into a general rule — the ask is to make one claim mechanically checkable.
cases.wrong_if: claim-to-fixture is a checkability move, not a breadth move
